This standard has been prepared to standardize the closed type shuttle race assembly fitting and functioning with other mating components of sewing machine.

IS 13806 : 1993 4 MATERIALS 4.1 The material for the closed is specified as follows. type shuttle race 5 DIMENSIONS AND TOLERANCES

The fitting dimensions and tolerances of shuttle race as indicated in Fig. 2 shall conform to values as given in Table I. 6 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH

4.1.1 The shuttle race body shall be made from cast iron of suitable grade such as FG 150 of IS 210 : 1978. 4.1.2 The shuttle race ring shall be made from case hardening steel designation 20MnXr5 of IS 4432 : 1988 so as to achieve a hardness of 450 HV in the finished state [ see IS 1501 ( Part 1 ) : 1984 I. 4.1.3 The shuttle race ring spring and tnp plate may be designed as per IS 10878 ( Part 1 ) : 1984 and IS 10878 ( Part 2 ) : 1984. Material used for spring shall conform to IS 2507 : 1975. These shall be hardened and tempered. 4.1.4 The pins and all screws to be used for closed type shuttle race assembly shall be made of mild steel and shall be case hardened.

6.1 Surface on sliding parts and thread passage for shuttle race shall be polished to smooth surface/edges to avoid breakage/damage to threads, while stitching. 6.2 The external visible surface shall have bright nickle/chromium plated finish. All other components of race assembly including screws, pins and ring etc. shall have nickle plated/blackened Service surface finis!1 conforming to at least Grade No. 1 with Designation Fe/NilOb Cr r of IS 1068 : 1993. 6.3 Shuttle groove diameter `F' shall be concentric to diameter `D' and `E' of spigot for mounting shuttle race on bed within 0'3 mm ( TIR ).

IS 13806 : 1993 7 SAMPLING Unless otherwise agreed to between the supplier and the purchaser the sampling plan as given in Annex A shall be followed. For further information reference may be made to IS 2500 (Part 1 ) : 1973. 8 MARKING Unless o!herwise and manufacturer, agreed to between the purchaser the shuttle race may be marked with the source 9 PACKING Each closed type shuttle race assembly shall be given a suitable antirust coating, packed in a polyethylene bag and then put in a card board carton bearing manufacturer's name or trade mark, type and description of contents. The wrapped, closed type shuttle race shall be securely packed in accordance with best prevailent trade practice. of manufacture or trade mark.

ANNEX A ( CIuuse 7 )
SCALE A-l SCALE OF SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY

OF SAMPLING

A-l.1 In any consignment all the shuttle races of the same type and manufactured from the same material under essentially similar conditions of manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. A-l.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements ot specification, tests shall be carried out for each lot separately. The number of shuttle races to be selected at random for this purpose shall be in accordance with co1 1 and 2 of Table 2. A-l.3 If the shuttle races are packed in order to ensure the randomness IS 4905 : 1968 shall be used. individually, of selection

dimensions and tolerance ( see 5 ) and workmanship and finish (see 6 ). If the number of shuttle races failing to meet one or more of the requirements mentioned above is less than or equal to the permissible number of defectives given in co1 3 of Table 2, the lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of these characteristics. A-l.4 If the shuttle races are packed in different cartons, a suitable number of cartons ( not less than 20 percent of the tctal in the lot subject to a minimum of 2 ) shall be chosen at random. From each of the cartons so chosen, an approximately equal number of shuttle races shall be picked up from its different parts so as to obtain the required number of shuttle races specified in col 2 of Table 2. Standard

Mark

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS. Review of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards Monthly Additions'.
